## SCHOLARLY + DS&A CONTEXT
# ALGORITHM: KR-20 reliability
#   source:      journey-os-algorithms-scholarly.html §IX
#   complexity:  time O(n*k) · space O(k) where n=students, k=items
#   parameters:
#     - formula: KR-20 = (k / (k-1)) * (1 - sum(pi * qi) / variance_total)
#     - pi = proportion correct for item i
#     - qi = 1 - pi
#     - variance_total = variance of total scores across students
#     - threshold: >= 0.70 for high-stakes exams
#     - minimum sample: >= 10 students (below this, KR-20 is unreliable)
#   security:    N/A
#   invariants:
#     - KR-20 always in [0.0, 1.0] for well-formed data
#     - KR-20 < 0.70 on high-stakes exam triggers warning flag
#     - KR-20 not computed if n_students < 10 (returns null with reason)
#     - Items with zero variance excluded from computation
#
# FOUNDATION: Kuder & Richardson, 1937
#   claim:   KR-20 measures internal consistency reliability for dichotomous items
#   rule:    Only applies to binary (correct/incorrect) scoring — not partial credit
#   applies: features/analytics/services/ReliabilityService.ts
#
# FOUNDATION: Nunnally, 1978
#   claim:   Reliability >= 0.70 is acceptable for research; >= 0.80 for high-stakes decisions
#   rule:    Flag exams below 0.70; warning for exams below 0.80 used for grading
#   applies: features/analytics/services/ReliabilityService.ts → threshold checks

## Summary
Implement KR-20 internal consistency reliability computation for exams, with threshold warnings for high-stakes assessments and a dashboard panel showing reliability metrics.

## User story
As a faculty member, I want to see the KR-20 reliability coefficient for each exam, so that I can assess whether the exam is internally consistent enough for high-stakes grading decisions.

## Why this matters
An unreliable exam (KR-20 < 0.70) means student scores contain too much measurement error for fair grading decisions. Without this metric, MSM cannot demonstrate to LCME that their assessments meet psychometric standards. An incorrect KR-20 computation (e.g., including zero-variance items, computing on < 10 students) would give false confidence in bad exams.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ReliabilityService.computeKR20() implements the exact formula: (k/(k-1)) * (1 - sum(pi*qi) / variance)
- [ ] Returns null with reason string when n_students < 10
- [ ] Excludes items with zero variance from computation (all correct or all incorrect)
- [ ] Flags exams with KR-20 < 0.70 as "below_threshold"
- [ ] Flags exams with KR-20 < 0.80 that are tagged high-stakes as "marginal_reliability"
- [ ] KR20Panel displays: KR-20 value, threshold indicator (green/yellow/red), student count, excluded item count
- [ ] KR20Panel integrates into ItemAnalyticsDashboard as a summary panel
- [ ] Unit tests verify computation against known textbook examples

## Schema changes
```sql
-- Add reliability column to a new exam_reliability table
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS exam_reliability (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  exam_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES exams(id) UNIQUE,
  kr20 NUMERIC(5,4) CHECK (kr20 BETWEEN 0 AND 1),
  n_students INTEGER NOT NULL,
  n_items INTEGER NOT NULL,
  n_items_excluded INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  flags TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  reason TEXT,
  computed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  institution_id UUID NOT NULL
);

ALTER TABLE exam_reliability ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY "Faculty and admin read exam_reliability"
  ON exam_reliability FOR SELECT
  USING (institution_id = auth.jwt() ->> 'institution_id');

-- After adding: pnpm db:types to regenerate database.generated.ts
```

// Pattern: Pure computation service (no side effects, easily testable)
// features/analytics/services/ReliabilityService.ts

export class ReliabilityService {
  static readonly MIN_STUDENTS = 10;
  static readonly HIGH_STAKES_THRESHOLD = 0.70;
  static readonly RECOMMENDED_THRESHOLD = 0.80;

  static computeKR20(itemScores: boolean[][]): {
    kr20: number | null;
    nStudents: number;
    nItems: number;
    nItemsExcluded: number;
    reason: string | null;
  } {
    const nStudents = itemScores.length;
    if (nStudents < this.MIN_STUDENTS) {
      return { kr20: null, nStudents, nItems: 0, nItemsExcluded: 0, reason: 'Fewer than 10 students' };
    }

}

// tests/E09/E09-S02.api.test.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('KR-20 computed correctly for known textbook example', async () => {
  // 5-item test, 20 students — known KR-20 = 0.72
  const { ReliabilityService } = await import(
    '../../features/analytics/services/ReliabilityService'
  );
  const itemScores = /* textbook dataset */;
  const result = ReliabilityService.computeKR20(itemScores);
  expect(result.kr20).toBeCloseTo(0.72, 2);
});

test('KR-20 returns null for fewer than 10 students', async () => {
  const { ReliabilityService } = await import(
    '../../features/analytics/services/ReliabilityService'
  );
  const itemScores = Array(5).fill([true, false, true]); // only 3 students
  const result = ReliabilityService.computeKR20(itemScores);
  expect(result.kr20).toBeNull();
  expect(result.reason).toContain('10 students');
});

test('KR-20 excludes zero-variance items', async () => {
  const { ReliabilityService } = await import(
    '../../features/analytics/services/ReliabilityService'
  );
  // Create dataset where item 0 is all-correct (zero variance)
  const itemScores = /* dataset with one zero-variance item */;
  const result = ReliabilityService.computeKR20(itemScores);
  expect(result.nItemsExcluded).toBe(1);
});

test('API returns reliability section in analytics response', async ({ request }) => {
  const { token } = await getTestToken(request, 'faculty');
  const res = await request.get('/api/admin/analytics/items?exam_id=test-exam-id', {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
  });
  expect(res.status()).toBe(200);
  const { data } = await res.json();
  expect(data.reliability).toBeDefined();
  expect(data.reliability.threshold_status).toBeDefined();
});
